verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Term by term the two agree: `logPowerWeight (C j m) (p j m) (g j / 2) q` unfolds to C_{j,m}·(1+|log q|)^{P_{j,m}}·q^{g_j/2}, and the paper fixes Λ_log(q) = 1 + |log q| on p. 56, so the base, the logarithmic exponent and the power g_j/2 match; the right-hand side (1/2)^j is 2^{-j}; the q-range q ≤ 1/(a j) is the paper's 0 < q ≤ a_j^{-1}; and the positivity hypothesis `hg : ∀ j, 1 ≤ j → 0 < g j` is the paper's 'each holds for all sufficiently small q because g_j > 0'. The Lean is stronger on three counts: it imposes the bound for every m ≤ j + 2 rather than m ≤ j; it bounds the absolute value, so the statement survives negative constants; and it delivers the surrounding recursion in the same existence statement (2·a_j ≤ a_{j+1}, which is the paper's a_{j+1} ≥ 2a_j; strict monotonicity; 1/a_j eventually below any fixed q, which is the paper's local finiteness; and B ≤ a_0, which supplies the paper's a_1^{-1} < q_0). The witness is an integer sequence where the paper's a_j are reals, which narrows the witness rather than the claim. The Lean's own docstring attributes this to 'Lemma 11.3 of the candidate manuscript', a numbering that does not match this manuscript.
